title: Short-term-rental operator role and contact review
hypothesis: An official STR permit establishes only a permit/license-holder or published permit-contact candidate. An owner-deliverable workflow requires separate current-owner evidence and an explicitly published business-contact fact; host, contact, manager, property owner, and license holder roles are not interchangeable.
ownerSource: NOLA and Orlando STR registers publish permit/license-holder and contact-related fields, but neither implemented parser records independent evidence that a named person currently owns the operating STR business.
phoneSource: The NOLA contact_phone and Orlando license_holder_phone fields are publicly published permit fields. The reviewed catalog/schema does not establish that every such field is an explicitly published business contact or that it belongs to the business owner; property-owner addresses and private-contact enrichment are excluded.

workflow.label: Official STR permit row
workflow.detail: Read only the public NOLA or Orlando permit/license row and its published fields. Do not use a property-owner address, parcel, residence, or private-phone lookup.

workflow.label: Current issued/active status?
workflow.detail: NOLA must be Issued and Orlando Active. A pending, closed, inactive, or other status is not a deliverable operating record.

workflow.label: Hold noncurrent permit
workflow.detail: Keep pending or non-active rows as non-deliverable source evidence.

workflow.label: Holder and contact roles align?
workflow.detail: Retain permit contact, license holder, and property-owner roles separately. A differing contact may be a manager or co-host and cannot replace the holder as owner identity.

workflow.label: Hold manager/contact-only role
workflow.detail: Do not call a contact, host, manager, property owner, or entity representative the operating business owner from role text alone.

workflow.label: Permit-holder candidate
workflow.detail: An issued/active person holder or aligned permit contact is an identity candidate only; it does not prove business ownership or handset relationship.

workflow.label: Explicit published business contact?
workflow.detail: Require affirmative source evidence that the phone is published for business contact. A public permit phone or a mobile classification alone is insufficient.

workflow.label: Hold nonbusiness or unknown contact
workflow.detail: Do not use a personal/residential contact, property address, skip trace, append, or phone lookup to create business-contact evidence.

workflow.label: Current owner relationship supported?
workflow.detail: Require independent, current evidence that the candidate owns the operating STR business; a license/permit-holder field alone does not satisfy this gate.

workflow.label: Hold owner-unconfirmed candidate
workflow.detail: Keep candidate-only, host, manager, and unresolved license-holder rows out of owner delivery.

workflow.label: Verify contact and compliance
workflow.detail: After both role gates pass, record line type, reachability, DNC/TCPA, suppression, freshness, and handset relationship independently.

workflow.label: Hold failed verification
workflow.detail: Hold non-mobile, unreachable, suppressed, stale, or otherwise unsupported records.

workflow.label: Deliver supported owner classification
workflow.detail: Only current ownership, explicit business-contact publication, and all verification/compliance gates support owner delivery.

edges.label: personal, residential, or unknown publication role
all contact and compliance gates pass

failures.risk: The NOLA parser accepts Pending applications as well as Issued permits.
failures.mitigation: Restrict nolaStrRow to Issued and retain Pending as non-deliverable source evidence.

failures.risk: A NOLA permit contact who differs from the license holder can become the lead identity, despite possibly being a manager or co-host.
failures.mitigation: Persist contact and holder roles, do not substitute a differing contact for the holder, and hold unresolved roles from owner delivery.

failures.risk: A permit/license holder is treated as proof of current ownership of the operating STR business.
failures.mitigation: Require independently recorded, current owner evidence before owner delivery; retain permit evidence as candidate-only otherwise.

failures.risk: A publicly listed permit phone is treated as an explicitly published business contact without a source role fact.
failures.mitigation: Require affirmative business-contact publication evidence and keep unknown/personal contact roles held; mobile verification does not repair source-role evidence.

failures.risk: Property-owner names or addresses become a route to residential lookup, parcel work, skip trace, or private-phone append.
failures.mitigation: Do not use those fields for contact discovery or matching. The workflow is restricted to explicit published business-contact evidence.

sources.scope: Row-level facts needed for owner delivery without residential/private-contact enrichment.

iterations.hypothesis: The live STR recipe C distinguishes current operators/owners from permit contacts and excludes noncurrent applications before delivery.
iterations.test: Offline five-case parser audit on 2026-09-24 using nolaStrRow and orlandoStrRow only: issued same contact/holder; issued differing contact/holder; pending same contact/holder; issued entity holder with person contact; active Orlando person holder with entity property owner. Placeholder values only; no network, paid call, secret, real contact, or property lookup.
iterations.observed: All five synthetic rows were accepted. NOLA accepted Pending and selected a person-shaped contact even when it differed from a person holder or when the holder was an entity; Orlando accepted the person holder while a distinct entity property owner was present. The generic recipe-C path selects non-null phones for verification and has no STR owner/business-contact role gate. This measures code behavior only, not source coverage, ownership, line type, reachability, DNC/TCPA, or delivery.
iterations.change: Mark the workflow partial and propose an issued-only NOLA gate, role retention without contact substitution, and a delivery hold pending independently supported current ownership plus explicit published-business-contact evidence. Keep property/residential and private-phone enrichment outside scope.

measurement.result: Five synthetic parser cases were all accepted: NOLA issued same-holder/contact, NOLA issued differing contact/holder, NOLA Pending, NOLA issued entity-holder/person-contact, and Orlando Active person-holder/entity-property-owner. Fixture/code audit only; no live rows, personal contacts, phone values, ownership checks, reachability, DNC/TCPA, or delivery measurements.

cost.basis: Offline fixture/code audit only; no provider request, paid verification, append, property lookup, or private-contact enrichment was invoked.
cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. The brain's STR research estimate and historical economics use another denominator and do not establish owner-delivery cost.

implementation.summary: NOLA and Orlando adapters are implemented and mapped to recipe C. NOLA accepts Pending and substitutes a person-shaped permit contact for the holder; generic register-phone verification/delivery has no STR-specific current-owner or explicit-business-contact gate. Property-owner/residential data remains outside the permitted workflow.

nextMeasurement: After the shared correction, rerun the five synthetic cases: only an Issued/Active row with separate role facts can enter candidate review; Pending, entity-contact-only, and differing contact/holder cases must hold. Before any live contact study, obtain explicit approval for a lawful source with documented business-contact publication and current-owner facts, then measure business fit, role/ownership, line type, DNC/TCPA, reachability, suppression, and delivery under separate denominators without residential/private-phone enrichment.
